title: Multiplication: Equal Groups and Times Tables
seo_title: Multiplication – Primary 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Understand multiplication as repeated addition and equal groups; use arrays; know the 2, 5 and 10 times tables. (summary of the NERDC Primary 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 maths worksheets on multiplication: equal groups, repeated addition, arrays and the 2, 5 and 10 times tables. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
  • An array shows rows and columns. 2 rows of 5 = 2 × 5 = 10.
  • Learn the 2, 5 and 10 times tables by counting in 2s, 5s and 10s.

Examples

Example

4 groups of 5

5 + 5 + 5 + 5

Answer: 4 × 5 = 20

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the two numbers3 × 4 = 12, not 7.
Groups that are not equalEvery group must be the same.
Counting rows onlyCount the rows and the columns.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 3 groups. 2 is how many counters are in each group.
Count the rings: there are 4 groups. 5 is how many stars are in each group.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 5 groups. 3 is how many blocks are in each group.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Look inside one ring. It has 5 counters. Every group is the same.
Look inside one ring. It has 4 stars. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many blocks are in each group?
items.e: Look inside one ring. It has 2 blocks. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: 2 groups of 3. Count in 3s: 3, 6. There are 6. (Not 2 + 3 = 5: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)
5 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10. (Not 5 + 2 = 7: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)

items.q: How many blocks are there altogether?
items.e: 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. There are 15. (Not 3 + 5 = 8: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: 2 groups of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20. There are 20. (Not 2 + 10 = 12: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)
There are 3 groups. Each group has 4. Add 4, 3 times: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 5. Add 5, 4 times: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 5 groups. Each group has 2. Add 2, 5 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.
2 groups of 4 is written 2 × 4. It means 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: 3 groups of 10 is written 3 × 10. It means 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.

items.q: Which addition adds the rows?
items.e: There are 3 rows. Each row has 4. So add 4, 3 times: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
There are 2 rows. Each row has 5. So add 5, 2 times: 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Which addition adds the rows?
items.e: There are 4 rows. Each row has 3. So add 3, 4 times: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12.

items.q: Which addition adds the rows?
items.e: There are 5 rows. Each row has 2. So add 2, 5 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.
There are 3 rows. Each row has 5. So add 5, 3 times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: How many rows are in this array?
items.e: Rows go across. Count from top to bottom: 3 rows. Each row has 5.
Columns go up and down. Count from left to right: 4 columns. Each column has 2.

items.q: How many blocks are in the array?
items.e: 2 rows of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. That is 10. It is 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: How many counters are in the array?
items.e: 4 rows of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8. It is 4 × 2 = 8.
3 rows of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. That is 30. It is 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q: How many blocks are in the array?
items.e: 5 rows of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25. It is 5 × 5 = 25.

items.q: Which two number sentences match this array?
items.e: Rows: 2 rows of 5 is 2 × 5. Columns: 5 columns of 2 is 5 × 2. Both are 10, so both match.
Rows: 3 rows of 2 is 3 × 2. Columns: 2 columns of 3 is 2 × 3. Both are 6, so both match.
Rows: 5 rows of 10 is 5 × 10. Columns: 10 columns of 5 is 10 × 5. Both are 50, so both match.
You can multiply in any order. 5 × 2 and 2 × 5 are the same array turned round. So 2 × 5 = 10 too.
Rows go across. Count them from top to bottom: there are 3 rows. Each row has 5 dots, but 5 is the number of columns.
Rows go across. Count them from top to bottom: there are 2 rows. Each row has 4 stars, but 4 is the number of columns.

items.q: How many rows are in this array?
items.e: Rows go across. Count them from top to bottom: there are 4 rows. Each row has 3 squares, but 3 is the number of columns.

items.q: How many rows are in this array?
items.e: Rows go across. Count them from top to bottom: there are 5 rows. Each row has 2 dots, but 2 is the number of columns.
Columns go up and down. Count them from left to right: there are 5 columns. 2 is the number of rows.

items.q: How many columns are in this array?
items.e: Columns go up and down. Count them from left to right: there are 2 columns. 4 is the number of rows.

items.q: How many columns are in this array?
items.e: Columns go up and down. Count them from left to right: there are 4 columns. 3 is the number of rows.
Columns go up and down. Count them from left to right: there are 3 columns. 5 is the number of rows.

items.q: How many squares are in each row?
items.e: Look at one row, across. It has 5 squares. Every row has the same number.

items.q: How many dots are in each row?
items.e: Look at one row, across. It has 3 dots. Every row has the same number.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. 4 × 2 = 8.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: How many counters are there?
How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. 3 × 2 = 6.

items.q: Which matches the picture?
items.e: There are 5 groups with 2 counters in each group: 5 × 2 = 10. 5 + 2 adds the numbers. It does not count the groups.

items.q: Which matches the picture?
items.e: There are 7 groups with 2 counters in each group: 7 × 2 = 14. 7 + 2 adds the numbers. It does not count the groups.

items.q:
Count in 2s. What comes next?
6, 8, 10, ?
items.e: Each number is 2 more than the one before: 10 + 2 = 12. So 2 × 6 = 12.

items.q:
Count in 2s. What comes next?
14, 16, 18, ?
items.e: Each number is 2 more than the one before: 18 + 2 = 20. So 2 × 10 = 20.

items.q: Socks come in pairs. How many socks are in 8 pairs?
items.e: A pair is 2. 8 pairs is 8 × 2. Double 8: 8 + 8 = 16. 10 is 8 + 2, which adds instead of multiplies.
Times 2 means double. Double 9: 9 + 9 = 18.
Times 2 means double. Double 3: 3 + 3 = 6.
Times 2 means double. Double 5: 5 + 5 = 10.
Times 2 means double. Double 6: 6 + 6 = 12.
Times 2 means double. Double 4: 4 + 4 = 8.
Times 2 means double. Double 8: 8 + 8 = 16.
Times 2 means double. Double 7: 7 + 7 = 14.
Times 2 means double. Double 11: 11 + 11 = 22.
Times 2 means double. Double 12: 12 + 12 = 24.

items.q: Which number is in the 2 times table?
items.e: Numbers in the 2 times table are even. They end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. 16 is in the 2 times table.

items.q: Which number is not in the 2 times table?
items.e: Numbers in the 2 times table are even. They end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. 15 is not in the 2 times table.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: Each hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers are there?
items.e: 4 hands of 5 fingers: 5, 10, 15, 20. 4 × 5 = 20. 9 is 4 + 5, which adds instead.

items.q: The red hand is the minute hand. How many minutes past 3 is it?
items.e: The minute hand points to 4. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 minutes past 3.

items.q: The red hand is the minute hand. How many minutes past 2 is it?
items.e: The minute hand points to 9. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. So it is 45 minutes past 2.

items.q:
Count in 5s. What comes next?
15, 20, 25, ?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 25 + 5 = 30. So 5 × 6 = 30.

items.q:
Count in 5s. What comes next?
40, 45, 50, ?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 50 + 5 = 55. So 5 × 11 = 55.
Count in 5s, 4 times: 5, 10, 15, 20. So the answer is 20.
Count in 5s, 5 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. So the answer is 25.
Count in 5s, 8 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. So the answer is 40.
Count in 5s, 9 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. So the answer is 45.
Count in 5s, 7 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So the answer is 35.
Count in 5s, 10 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. So the answer is 50.

items.q: Which number is in the 5 times table?
items.e: Numbers in the 5 times table end in 0 or 5. 45 is in the 5 times table.

items.q: Which number is not in the 5 times table?
items.e: Numbers in the 5 times table end in 0 or 5. 52 is not in the 5 times table.
Count in 5s, 10 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. So the answer is 50.
Count in 5s, 4 times: 5, 10, 15, 20. So the answer is 20.
Count in 5s, 7 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So the answer is 35.

items.q: How many cubes are there?
items.e: Each rod is 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. 4 tens = 40.

items.q: How many cubes are there?
items.e: Each rod is 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. 7 tens = 70.

items.q: How many cubes are there?

Count in 10s. What comes next?
30, 40, 50, ?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before: 50 + 10 = 60. So 10 × 6 = 60.

items.q:
Count in 10s. What comes next?
60, 70, 80, ?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before: 80 + 10 = 90. So 10 × 9 = 90.
3 tens make 30. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. So the answer is 30.
7 tens make 70. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. So the answer is 70.
9 tens make 90. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. So the answer is 90.
6 tens make 60. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. So the answer is 60.
4 tens make 40. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. So the answer is 40.
8 tens make 80. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80. So the answer is 80.
Ask: what times 10 makes 50? 5 tens make 50, so ? = 5. Check: 5 × 10 = 50.
You can swap the numbers in a multiplication. 10 × 4 = 40 and 4 × 10 = 40. So ? = 10.

items.q: Which number is in the 10 times table?
items.e: Numbers in the 10 times table end in 0. 70 is in the 10 times table.

items.q: Which number is not in the 10 times table?
items.e: Numbers in the 10 times table end in 0. 55 is not in the 10 times table.

items.q: Which number is in the 2, the 5 and the 10 times tables?
items.e: 30 ends in 0, so it is in all three: 2 × 15, 5 × 6 and 10 × 3. 25 and 15 are only in the 5 times table. 12 is only in the 2 times table.
4 tens make 40. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. So the answer is 40.
9 tens make 90. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. So the answer is 90.
6 tens make 60. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. So the answer is 60.
